html:
SMTO-EXE-0024 — This prompt can't be saved to Fast Cache

GUID: 45894a3c-ea39-4de4-946e-6cacc9ed09b1
Slug: cache-pin-unavailable
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO checked this task and found it isn't safe to save for reuse, for example because it changed things, a step failed, or it relied on web results. Nothing was saved, and the original task is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Point at the Pin prompt to Fast Cache button next to your prompt to read why it was refused. The reason tells you whether this task could ever qualify; a task that changes things never will.
  2. If a step failed or was stopped, run the task again until it finishes cleanly, then try pinning that new run. Only tasks that finished successfully and only looked up information can be saved for reuse.
  3. Otherwise, just send the prompt as usual whenever you need it. Without a Fast Cache entry, SMTO runs the task normally with all its usual checks.

What success looks like

  • The pin button shows a check mark (Pinned to Fast Cache), or the task runs normally without a pin.

If it still fails

  • If a task that only looked things up and finished cleanly still can't be pinned, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to get around this check; it keeps unsafe steps from being reused.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Fast Cache management rejected the pin or inspect request with a Discard reason (for example write_effect, operation_failed, unproven_dependency, web_only_evidence or scope_mismatch) because the execution is not eligible for safe reuse.

What this means

  • Cache management received a Discard eligibility decision and returned its reason instead of creating or changing an unsafe reusable execution entry. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Cache management received a Discard eligibility decision and returned its reason instead of creating or changing an unsafe reusable execution entry.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the specific Discard reason and accepted execution evidence before changing or pinning the entry.

How to fix it

  • Read the Discard reason in the 409/404 detail (error_ref cache_pin_unavailable) to see which eligibility check failed. Use ordinary execution for ineligible procedures, or pin a later run that completed successfully with read-only, proven steps; do not relax validation to make it cacheable.
  • Inspect its current eligibility reason. Use ordinary execution when the procedure cannot be safely reused; do not relax validation to make it cacheable.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A procedure that meets the current eligibility checks is accepted, or ordinary execution handles the task.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
